question_text: If 5 government employees can process 75 applications in 3 days, how many applications can 8 employees process in the same number of days?

hint_ladder.title: Find the Unit Rate First
hint_ladder.text: When you have a group doing work in the same time, find the per-person output. For 5 people doing 75 apps, each does how many?

hint_ladder.title: The Simple Division
hint_ladder.text: Divide 75 by 5 to get 15 applications per employee in 3 days. That’s your key number.

hint_ladder.title: Now Scale Up
hint_ladder.text: Now with 8 employees, multiply the per-person output (15) by 8. 15 × 8 = 120 applications.

hint_ladder.title: Almost There
hint_ladder.text: You’ve got 120. Avoid traps: adding extra employees doesn’t mean adding a random number. Trust the per-unit method.

next_time_rule: For constant-time direct proportion, find per-person output first; it's your scaling key. Never just add to the total.
deconstruct_text:
Example: Sa Barangay San Roque, 5 employees processed 75 applications for their clearance drive in 3 days. Since time is the same, hanapin muna natin ang kaya ng isang tao.

75 divided by 5 equals 15. So bawat isang empleyado, 15 applications ang kaya sa 3 araw.

Ngayon, kung 8 na sila, multiply lang: 15 x 8 = 120 applications.

Tandaan: always hanapin ang per-unit output. Parang kita ng isang tricycle driver sa isang araw—madali nang malaman kita ng walong drivers kapag alam mo ang per driver. Kaya iwasan magdagdag na lang basta. You got this!
